newsitem.title: USA: U.S. investigators may dredge for TWA wreckage.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investigators may dredge for TWA wreckage.

text.p: Investigators may dredge the Atlantic Ocean floor for more wreckage of TWA Flight 800 in an effort to learn what caused the plane to crash, U.S. Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick said on Thursday.

"We are considering dredging," she told the weekly Justice Department news conference when asked about the investigation into the July 17 explosion of the Paris-bound jetliner shortly after takeoff from Kennedy International Airport.

"Even a small hole in the plane could cause the crash...and it is for that reason that recovery of as much of the plane -- wreckage -- as possible is necessary," Gorelick said. She added that it could be an eight-inch (20 cm) or 10-inch (25 cm) hole.
"So we are going to take every step we possibly can to bring up absolutely every piece of the plane," she said.
Investigators are trying to determine whether a bomb, a missile or mechanical failure caused the jet to crash off Long Island, New York, killing all 230 people on board.
"If you were looking for evidence of a bomb or missile, you could be looking for a very small piece of the plane that would give you an indication of such an occurrence," she said.
The entire section of the plane where the explosion occurred has to be recovered before investigators can pinpoint what caused the crash, Gorelick said.
Investigators are re-assembling the plane in an old aircraft hangar in Calverton, New York.
